Cross-platform numerical consistency in bgms. Source:
`src/math/custom_explog.h`, `custom_explog.cpp`,
`custom_arma_explog.h`, and `explog_macros.h`.

## The problem

Standard library implementations of `exp()` and `log()` differ across
platforms. The GNU C Library (glibc, used on Linux), macOS libm, and
MSVC's C runtime produce slightly different results for the same
input, especially near boundary values. These differences are small
(last-bit-of-precision level) but compound across thousands of MCMC
iterations, causing:

- Different platforms to produce different posterior samples from the
  same seed
- CRAN check failures when comparing numerical output across
  architectures
- Occasional test failures when expected values are computed on one
  platform and checked on another

## OpenLibM solution

bgms ships a copy of the `__ieee754_exp()` and `__ieee754_log()`
implementations from OpenLibM (the FreeBSD/Sun math library). These
are self-contained C functions that follow IEEE 754 exactly and
produce identical results on all platforms.

The implementation in `custom_explog.cpp` (approximately 800 lines)
is the original Sun/FreeBSD code, lightly adapted to compile as C++
within an R package.

## Platform detection

The macro system in `explog_macros.h` controls when custom exp/log
is used:

```cpp
#if (defined(_WIN32) && (!defined(CUSTOM_EXP_LOG) || CUSTOM_EXP_LOG == 0)) \
  || (!defined(_WIN32) && defined(CUSTOM_EXP_LOG) && CUSTOM_EXP_LOG != 0)
  #define USE_CUSTOM_LOG 1
#endif
```

The logic:

- **Windows** — Uses custom exp/log by default because MSVC's
  `std::exp`/`std::log` differ from POSIX implementations and are
  slower
- **Linux/macOS** — Uses the system libm by default (which is fast
  and POSIX-compliant). Custom exp/log can be enabled by setting
  `CUSTOM_EXP_LOG=1`

The `configure` and `configure.win` scripts set the appropriate
compiler flag in `Makevars`.

## Usage in C++ code

Two levels of macros are available:

| Macro | Expands to (custom) | Expands to (system) |
|-------|-------------------|-------------------|
| `MY_EXP(x)` | `__ieee754_exp(x)` | `std::exp(x)` |
| `ARMA_MY_EXP(X)` | `custom_arma_exp(X)` | `arma::exp(X)` |

The `ARMA_MY_EXP` variant applies element-wise custom exp/log to
Armadillo matrices and vectors. It wraps `custom_arma_exp()` and
`custom_arma_log()` from `custom_arma_explog.h`, which iterate over
matrix elements and call the scalar `__ieee754_exp`/`__ieee754_log`.

## Performance

On macOS and Linux, the system `exp()` and `log()` are highly
optimized (hardware-accelerated on some architectures). The custom
versions are slightly slower but guarantee cross-platform
reproducibility.

On Windows with MSVC, the custom implementations are often 2–5×
*faster* than `std::exp`/`std::log`, making the custom path
beneficial for both correctness and speed.

## EXP_BOUND and overflow prevention

The [variable helpers](variable-helpers.qmd) use `EXP_BOUND = 709`
as the threshold for safe exponentiation, derived from the IEEE 754
double-precision range:

- $\exp(709) \approx 8.2 \times 10^{307}$ — largest representable
- $\exp(710) = +\text{Inf}$
- $\exp(-745) \approx 5 \times 10^{-324}$ — smallest positive subnormal
- $\exp(-746) = 0$

This bound is used throughout the codebase (not just in variable
helpers) to guard against overflow before calling `MY_EXP()`.

## R interface

The `explog_interface.cpp` file exposes the custom exp/log functions
to R for testing purposes. This allows verification that the custom
implementations match expected values in R-level unit tests.
